title: Pattern Intelligence: Unsupervised, LLM-Interpreted Discovery of Systematic Underpayment and Denial Patterns in Healthcare Revenue Cycle Management
abstract: arXiv:2610.27684v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Healthcare providers lose substantial revenue to systematic payer underpayments and claim denials, yet identifying the recurring, correctable patterns behind them remains largely manual and does not scale to hospital claim volumes. We present Pattern Intelligence, a deployed system that discovers such patterns without supervision by clustering claims on their adjudication behaviour rather than their identity. Each claim is embedded in a 130-dimensional vector combining per-line expected-versus-actual payment ratios, claim adjustment reason (CARC) codes, denial and payment signals, and service composition. Payer and contract identity are deliberately excluded from the distance metric - we show they dominate the geometry and collapse clusters into trivial per-payer groups - and are reintroduced only as a post-hoc segmentation (by contract and visit type) that keeps every surfaced pattern coherent and actionable. translated_title: 模式智能：医疗收入周期管理中系统性少付与拒付模式的无监督发现与LLM解读
translated_abstract: 医疗提供方因付款方系统性少付与索赔拒付而损失大量收入，然而识别其背后反复出现、可纠正的模式仍主要依赖人工，且无法扩展到医院级别的索赔量。我们提出Pattern Intelligence——一个已部署的系统，它通过基于索赔的裁决行为（而非索赔身份）进行聚类，以无监督方式发现此类模式。每个索赔被嵌入为一个130维向量，其中结合了逐行的预期与实际支付比率、索赔调整原因（CARC）代码、拒付与支付信号以及服务构成。我们刻意将付款方与合同身份排除在距离度量之外——我们证明它们会主导几何结构，使聚类退化为按付款方划分的平凡分组——并且仅在事后作为分割维度（按合同和就诊类型）重新引入，从而使每个被呈现出的模式保持连贯且可操作。我们使用HDBSCAN进行聚类……（原文摘要在此截断）
tldr: 该论文提出Pattern Intelligence系统：通过基于裁决行为（刻意排除付款方身份）的130维索赔嵌入与HDBSCAN无监督聚类，再将付款方与合同信息作为事后分割重新引入，并借助LLM进行解读，从而自动发现医疗收入周期管理中可纠正的系统性少付与拒付模式。
en_tdlr: Pattern Intelligence is a deployed unsupervised system that discovers correctable systematic underpayment and denial patterns in healthcare revenue cycle management by clustering claims on adjudication behavior via a 130-dimensional embedding with HDBSCAN—excluding payer identity from the metric to avoid trivial groupings—and reintroducing it only as post-hoc segmentation for coherent, actionable, LLM-interpretable patterns.
